messages:
eva: Quick callout — I sketched a RICE heatmap to decide next wave of model admits for Q2. Need a quick alignment on gates (customer demand vs cost vs eval pass rate).

sam: can you drop the matrix here?

eva: sure — pasted below. thinking we treat models in top-right as 'admit' and middle-right as 'canary'. low-impact but cheap ones might be 'auto-admit' if evals pass. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

```
# model | reach (customers) | impact (product fit) | confidence (eval pass%) | effort (infra + ops)
orca-mini | 2 | 2 | 90 | 1  -> R:4 I:4 C:3 E:1
llama3-70b | 8 | 7 | 60 | 8   -> R:56 I:56 C:42 E:8
mistral-instruct | 6 | 6 | 75 | 5 -> R:36 I:36 C:45 E:5
gpt-3.5-legacy | 4 | 5 | 95 | 3 -> R:20 I:25 C:47 E:3
quantized-llama | 5 | 4 | 70 | 2 -> R:25 I:20 C:35 E:2
```

Note: RICE derivation we used Reach*Impact*Confidence / Effort (normalized-ish).

mike: overall looks reasonable. my worry: llama3-70b effort spikes ops support and dedicated infra; if we push it now we may cannibalize MLP throughput.

tanya: customer ask backlog has 3 enterprise customers explicitly requesting Mistral flavors for lower token cost. that bumps reach for mistral-instruct.

aleks: eval notes — llama3-70b shows regressions on our safety evals vs. current prod baseline. confidence needs a penalty unless we fix prompts/filters.

sam: propose concrete gates: 1) eval pass >= 80% on core prompt set, 2) infra cost per 1k tokens <= X (we can set X in the ticket), 3) enterprise demand >= 2 paying customers OR low effort (effort<=2).

eva: agreed. also want a rollout policy: canary -> 10% routed w/ automatic fallback after 3min token-latency SLO breach OR error spike. tag release with `model_variant: canary`.

aleks: +1 for safety rollback rule. for llama3-70b, if safety regressions persist, we should not admit even if enterprise asks. better to ship a tuned variant or smaller distillation first.

sam: quick tiebreaker rule: when RICE close within 10%, prefer lower ops effort unless reach delta > 2 customers. keeps cost predictability.

mike: ops note — quantized-llama auto-admit is tempting but we need to ensure our kernel selection supports the quantization variant on all Dedicated shapes, else we'll break Dedicated SLAs. ops-bot: infra-check scheduled for tomorrow.

ops-bot: scheduled infra compatibility run for quantized-llama on p4a/gpu-fleet — results ETA 2024-05-03 18:00 UTC.

eva: next steps: 1) mike/aleks add safety fixes + eval run for llama3-70b, 2) tanya to confirm paying-customer list for mistral, 3) sam to open rollout policy + cost threshold ticket. I'll synthesize by EOD and post a Q2 admit heatmap.

sam: assigning tickets now, will link.

eva: thanks — if anyone objects to the gates above quickly say so, otherwise we'll treat this as our temporary sequencing rule for the sprint. :white_check_mark:
